Reviewed the kernel and the Triton-runner integration in detail. The direction is right — this is a real memory round-trip on the Triton runner, and the DeepGEMM runner already has its fused counterpart. But there are two blocking kernel-level issues (one of which just broke the H100 deepep CI in #30924 in exactly this form, root-caused in #32188) plus a few integration hazards. Details inline; summary below.

**Severity order**: F1 NaN sanitization (blocking) > F2 shuffle UB on straddling warps (blocking-ish) > F3 PDL read ordering > F4 fp8 `intermediate_cache2` downstream effects > F5/F6 robustness & maintainability nits.

**Open questions**
1. Was `filter_expert=True` (EP) covered by any e2e run? The GSM8K config (TP4/DP2) has `num_experts == num_local_experts`, so the filtered path only has synthetic unit tests.
2. Any e2e throughput number (decode tok/s before/after) on a Triton-runner fp8 model? The PR shows kernel-level wins only; at decode batch sizes launch overhead can eat the round-trip saving.
3. Suggest landing with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_ACT_QUANT` default **off** until F1/F2 are fixed and one full CI cycle has passed — this path is default-on for every fp8-block model on the Triton runner.
4. The branch predates #30924/#32072: `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` (your unfused reference) has since been rerouted to the unified JIT kernel, and file layouts moved. Please rebase and re-run the bit-exactness assertions.

**Test gaps**: (a) NaN/Inf poison test mirroring `test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_non_finite_inputs_are_sanitized`; (b) shapes with `hidden_dim % 256 == 128` (e.g. 128/384/1408) under filtering + a `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` pass; (c) `scale_ue8m0=True` has zero coverage and no integration caller — drop the axis or test it; (d) a capture+replay smoke test since the kernel launches with PDL inside decode graphs.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**[correctness, blocking] Non-finite inputs become fp8 NaN codes.** `__nv_fp8x4_e4m3(float4)` uses SATFINITE, which saturates ±inf/out-of-range but converts **NaN to an fp8 NaN code (0x7f)**. The absmax above uses `fmaxf` (IEEE drops the NaN operand), so `inv_scale` stays finite and NaN values sail straight into the packed codes.

Every kernel this path replaces (`silu_and_mul` + `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` — AOT v1/v2, Triton, and the unified kernel after #32188) clamps first: IEEE `fminf`/`fmaxf` return the non-NaN operand, so non-finite inputs quantize to ±448. CUDA-graph capture warmup runs the model over reused, uninitialized buffers; on CI runners those contain NaN bit patterns. Exactly this omission in #30924 broke the H100 deepep CI (`NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits`), root-caused and fixed in #32188 — and this kernel sits on the default Triton-runner path with the env flag default-on.

Fix (bit-identical for finite inputs): a single-sided `fminf(v, 448.f)` before packing is sufficient — see #32296 for the argument (min kills NaN/+inf, SATFINITE handles -inf). Also `scale = local_max / kFP8E4M3Max` (L134) can store an exact `0.0` scale for an all-zero group; the family computes `max(amax, eps) / 448` and never emits 0.0 — worth matching while here. Please also add a poison test mirroring `test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_non_finite_inputs_are_sanitized`.

**[correctness, blocking-ish] `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, ...)` with early-exited lanes is UB.** Two divergent `return`s sit above this (L89 tail, L92 expert filter). Whenever `hidden_dim % 256 == 128` (i.e. `num_vecs % 32 == 16`) a warp straddles two tokens, so half the warp can exit while the other half executes a shuffle whose mask names the exited lanes — undefined behavior per the CUDA programming guide, and `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` will flag it.

Note your own e2e config hits the shape: Qwen3-235B moe_inter 1536 / TP4 = 384 → `num_vecs = 48`. The minimal test shape `(1, 256)` hits it too (lanes 16–31 exit at the tail). It happens to produce correct results on sm90 because the xor-butterfly (masks 8/4/2/1) stays within each 16-lane half — that's luck, not contract, and it isn't guaranteed on future archs.

Suggested fix: keep all lanes alive through the reduce — follow the in-tree `per_token_group_quant` flat kernel pattern (warp-uniform exit + tail duplication via `min(work_id, total-1)`), or predicate the loads/stores instead of returning. Precedent for this bug class: #20661 (rmsnorm small-hidden fix).

**[PDL ordering]** `expert_ids` is read here, *before* `PDLWaitPrimary` (L99). With `enable_pdl(true)` this kernel may begin executing while the immediately-preceding kernel is still running; every dependent-data read must come after the wait. Today the preceding kernel is the Triton gate-up GEMM (produces `input`, which is correctly read after the wait) and `expert_ids` was produced earlier — safe by accident. Any reordering of the launch sequence turns this into a read of half-written data. Move the filter check below `PDLWaitPrimary`; zero cost. Same ordering rule as the masked `per_token_group_quant` kernel (wait precedes the `masked_m` read).

**[robustness]** The matchers pin shape/device but not dtype for `output_q`/`output_scale` (input does get `.with_dtype<T>()`). The kernel does raw pointer arithmetic assuming fp8/f32 contiguous rows — a wrong-dtype or non-contiguous buffer corrupts silently. Add `.with_dtype<fp8_e4m3_t>()` / `.with_dtype<float>()` and stride checks. Also `ActivationQuantParams.group_size` is dead in device code (the kernel hardcodes `kGroupSize = 128`) — drop the field or use it.

**[integration] Rebinding `intermediate_cache2` to fp8 has two downstream effects:**
1. `hooks.after_down(intermediate_cache2, ...)` (L805) now receives fp8 codes instead of bf16 activations when LoRA hooks are set — the `_use_fused_act_quant` gate doesn't exclude `hooks`. Either add `hooks is None` to the gate or confirm no hook consumes cache2 numerically.
2. The bf16 `intermediate_cache2` preallocated at L561 becomes a dead allocation on this path (`total_tokens * N/2 * 2` bytes allocated and dropped per layer/chunk). Hoist the `_use_fused_act_quant` decision above the allocation and skip it when the fused path will be taken.

+@cache_once
+def _jit_activation_quant_module(dtype: torch.dtype) -> Module:
+    args = make_cpp_args(dtype, is_arch_support_pdl())
+    return load_jit(
+        "fused_act_and_mul_quant",
+        *args,
+        cuda_files=["elementwise/fused_act_and_mul_quant.cuh"],
+        extra_cuda_cflags=_fast_math_flags(),
+        cuda_wrappers=[
+            (
+                "run_activation_quant",
+                f"ActivationQuantKernel<{args}>::run_activation_quant",
+            ),
+            (
+                "run_activation_quant_filtered",
+                f"ActivationQuantKernel<{args}>::run_activation_quant_filtered",
+            ),
+        ],
+    )
+
+
+@register_custom_op(mutates_args=["output_q", "output_scale"])
+def _run_activation_quant_inplace(
+    op_name: str,
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+    output_q: torch.Tensor,
+    output_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    group_size: int,
+    scale_ue8m0: bool,
+) -> None:
+    hidden_size = input.shape[-1] // 2
+    module = _jit_activation_quant_module(input.dtype)
+    input_2d = input.view(-1, hidden_size * 2)
+    output_q_2d = output_q.view(-1, hidden_size)
+    num_groups = hidden_size // group_size
+    output_scale_2d = output_scale.view(-1, num_groups)
+    module.run_activation_quant(
+        input_2d, output_q_2d, output_scale_2d, op_name, group_size, scale_ue8m0
+    )
+
+
+@register_custom_op(mutates_args=["output_q", "output_scale"])
+def _run_activation_quant_filtered_inplace(
+    op_name: str,
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+    output_q: torch.Tensor,
+    output_scale: torch.Tensor,
+    expert_ids: torch.Tensor,
+    expert_step: int,
+    group_size: int,
+    scale_ue8m0: bool,
+) -> None:
+    hidden_size = input.shape[-1] // 2
+    module = _jit_activation_quant_module(input.dtype)
+    input_2d = input.view(-1, hidden_size * 2)
+    output_q_2d = output_q.view(-1, hidden_size)
+    num_groups = hidden_size // group_size
+    output_scale_2d = output_scale.view(-1, num_groups)
+    module.run_activation_quant_filtered(
+        input_2d,
+        output_q_2d,
+        output_scale_2d,
+        expert_ids,
+        expert_step,

+def run_activation_quant(
+    op_name: str,
+    input: torch.Tensor,
+    output_q: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    output_scale: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    expert_ids: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
+    expert_step: int = 1,
+    group_size: int = 128,
+    scale_ue8m0: bool = False,
+) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Fused activation + per-token-group FP8 quantization.
+
+    Computes ``act(gate) * up`` and immediately quantizes the result to FP8
+    with per-group scales, saving one global memory round-trip compared to
+    calling :func:`run_activation` followed by a separate quantization step.
+
+    Args:
+        op_name: Activation type — one of ``"silu"``, ``"gelu"``, ``"gelu_tanh"``.
+        input: Input tensor of shape ``[*, 2 * hidden_dim]`` (gate||up concatenated).
+        output_q: Optional pre-allocated output for quantized values,
+            shape ``[*, hidden_dim]``, dtype ``torch.float8_e4m3fn``.
+        output_scale: Optional pre-allocated output for scales,
+            shape ``[*, hidden_dim // group_size]``, dtype ``torch.float32``.

+"""
+Correctness tests for the fused activation + per-token-group FP8 quantization JIT kernel.
+
+Validates against the unfused reference path:
+    act_out = run_activation(op_name, input)
+    ref_q, ref_scale = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(act_out, group_size)
+
+NOTE: The fused kernel keeps activation results in float32 registers before
+quantizing, while the unfused path truncates to bf16/fp16 between activation
+and quantization. This causes small numerical differences in scale (~1e-6)
+and occasionally different FP8 rounding for borderline values.
+"""
+
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.jit.utils import get_ci_test_range
+from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.activation import (
+    SUPPORTED_ACTIVATIONS,
+    run_activation,
+    run_activation_quant,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.fp8_kernel import sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=40, suite="nightly-kernel-1-gpu", nightly=True)
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Test parameters
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+OPS = list(SUPPORTED_ACTIVATIONS)  # ["silu", "gelu", "gelu_tanh"]
+DTYPES = [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16]
+GROUP_SIZE = 128
+
+# Shapes: (num_tokens, hidden_dim * 2).
+# hidden_dim must be divisible by GROUP_SIZE.
+SHAPES = get_ci_test_range(
+    full_range=[
+        (1, 256),  # minimal: hidden=128, 1 group per token
+        (7, 512),  # odd token count
+        (64, 1024),
+        (128, 2048),
+        (256, 4096),
+        (512, 8192),
+        (1024, 12288),  # large hidden (Llama-65B intermediate)
+        (4096, 2048),  # large token count
+    ],
+    ci_range=[
+        (1, 256),
+        (64, 1024),
+        (256, 4096),
+    ],
+)
+
+FILTER_SHAPES = get_ci_test_range(
+    full_range=[(128, 1024), (256, 2048), (512, 4096), (1024, 8192)],
+    ci_range=[(128, 1024), (256, 4096)],
+)
+EXPERT_STEPS = [1, 16]
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Tolerances: fused path keeps float32 precision through activation→quant,
+# while unfused truncates to bf16/fp16 in between. Scale differs by ~1e-5,
+# and FP8 values may differ by 1 ULP for borderline rounding.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+SCALE_ATOL = 0.0
+SCALE_RTOL = 0.0
+# FP8 E4M3: allow 1 ULP difference due to rounding tie-breaking between
+# different FP8 conversion paths (fp8_t(float) vs __nv_cvt_float2_to_fp8x2).
+FP8_MAX_DIFF_ULPS = 1
+
+
+def _assert_fp8_close(actual: torch.Tensor, expected: torch.Tensor) -> None:
+    """Assert FP8 tensors are within FP8_MAX_DIFF_ULPS of each other."""
+    diff = (actual.view(torch.uint8).int() - expected.view(torch.uint8).int()).abs()
+    max_diff = diff.max().item()
+    assert max_diff <= FP8_MAX_DIFF_ULPS, (
+        f"FP8 mismatch: max ULP diff = {max_diff}, "
+        f"mismatched elements = {(diff > FP8_MAX_DIFF_ULPS).sum().item()}/{diff.numel()}"
+    )
+
+
+def _reference_activation_quant(
+    op_name: str, input: torch.Tensor, group_size: int

+    act_out = run_activation(op_name, input, None)

+    """Fused kernel output must match unfused activation + quant."""

+
+    # Reference (unfused)

+

+
+    # Quantized values should match exactly (both use same rounding)

+    assert fused_q.shape == ref_q.shape

+
+    # Compare scales (small floating-point diff due to bf16 truncation in unfused path)

+    _assert_fp8_close(fused_q, ref_q)
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)

+    output_q = torch.empty(num_tokens, hidden, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
+    output_scale = torch.empty(

+    # Compare with reference

+    torch.testing.assert_close(

+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", FILTER_SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("expert_step", EXPERT_STEPS)
+def test_fused_act_quant_filter_expert(
+    op_name: str,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    shape: tuple[int, int],
+    expert_step: int,
+) -> None:
+    """Rows with expert_ids == -1 must leave output untouched (sentinel preserved)."""
+    num_tokens, dim = shape
+    hidden = dim // 2
+    input = torch.randn(num_tokens, dim, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+
+    # Pre-fill with sentinel
+    sentinel_q = torch.zeros(
+        num_tokens, hidden, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda"
+    )
+    sentinel_scale = torch.full(
+        (num_tokens, hidden // GROUP_SIZE),
+        float("nan"),
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    output_q = sentinel_q.clone()
+    output_scale = sentinel_scale.clone()
+
+    # Create expert_ids with some -1 entries
+    num_groups = (num_tokens + expert_step - 1) // expert_step
+    expert_ids = torch.randint(
+        low=0, high=8, size=(num_groups,), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"
+    )
+    skip_mask = torch.rand(num_groups, device="cuda") < 0.4
+    expert_ids[skip_mask] = -1
+
+    result_q, result_scale = run_activation_quant(
+        op_name,
+        input,
+        output_q=output_q,
+        output_scale=output_scale,
+        expert_ids=expert_ids,
+        expert_step=expert_step,
+        group_size=GROUP_SIZE,
+    )
+
+    # Check that skipped rows are untouched
+    token_skip = skip_mask[torch.arange(num_tokens, device="cuda") // expert_step]
+    if token_skip.any():
+        skipped_q = result_q[token_skip]
+        skipped_scale = result_scale[token_skip]
+        # quantized values should remain zero (sentinel)
+        assert torch.equal(
+            skipped_q.view(torch.uint8),
+            sentinel_q[token_skip].view(torch.uint8),
+        ), "fused kernel modified quantized output for skipped rows"
+        # scales should remain NaN (sentinel)
+        assert torch.isnan(
+            skipped_scale
+        ).all(), "fused kernel modified scale output for skipped rows"
+
+    # Check that non-skipped rows match the unfused reference
+    kept = ~token_skip
+    if kept.any():
+        # Run unfused reference on kept tokens only for comparison
+        ref_q, ref_scale = _reference_activation_quant(op_name, input, GROUP_SIZE)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            result_scale[kept], ref_scale[kept], atol=SCALE_ATOL, rtol=SCALE_RTOL
+        )
+        _assert_fp8_close(result_q[kept], ref_q[kept])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)
+def test_fused_act_quant_all_skipped(op_name: str) -> None:
+    """If every expert_id is -1, output must be entirely untouched."""
+    num_tokens, dim = 32, 1024
+    hidden = dim // 2
+    input = torch.randn(num_tokens, dim, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+
+    output_q = torch.zeros(num_tokens, hidden, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn, device="cuda")
+    output_scale = torch.full(
+        (num_tokens, hidden // GROUP_SIZE),
+        float("nan"),
+        dtype=torch.float32,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    orig_q = output_q.clone()
+
+    expert_ids = torch.full((num_tokens,), -1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    run_activation_quant(
+        op_name,
+        input,
+        output_q=output_q,
+        output_scale=output_scale,
+        expert_ids=expert_ids,
+        expert_step=1,
+        group_size=GROUP_SIZE,
+    )
+
+    assert torch.equal(output_q.view(torch.uint8), orig_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.isnan(output_scale).all()
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)
+def test_fused_act_quant_none_skipped(op_name: str) -> None:
+    """No -1 in expert_ids must yield identical output to unfiltered path."""
+    num_tokens, dim = 64, 2048
+    dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    input = torch.randn(num_tokens, dim, dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+
+    expert_ids = torch.zeros(num_tokens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    filtered_q, filtered_scale = run_activation_quant(
+        op_name,
+        input,
+        expert_ids=expert_ids,
+        expert_step=1,
+        group_size=GROUP_SIZE,
+    )
+    unfiltered_q, unfiltered_scale = run_activation_quant(
+        op_name,
+        input,
+        group_size=GROUP_SIZE,
+    )
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(filtered_scale, unfiltered_scale, atol=0.0, rtol=0.0)
+    assert torch.equal(filtered_q.view(torch.uint8), unfiltered_q.view(torch.uint8))
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Edge case tests
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)
+def test_fused_act_quant_single_token(op_name: str) -> None:
+    """Single-token input must work correctly."""
+    input = torch.randn(1, 256, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    fused_q, fused_scale = run_activation_quant(op_name, input, group_size=GROUP_SIZE)
+    ref_q, ref_scale = _reference_activation_quant(op_name, input, GROUP_SIZE)
+
+    torch.testing.assert_close(fused_scale, ref_scale, atol=SCALE_ATOL, rtol=SCALE_RTOL)
+    _assert_fp8_close(fused_q, ref_q)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("op_name", OPS)
+def test_fused_act_quant_zero_input(op_name: str) -> None:
+    """All-zero input should produce all-zero quantized output."""
+    input = torch.zeros(16, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    fused_q, fused_scale = run_activation_quant(op_name, input, group_size=GROUP_SIZE)
+    # act(0) * 0 = 0 for all activations, so quantized output should be 0
+    assert torch.equal(
+        fused_q.view(torch.uint8),
+        torch.zeros_like(fused_q).view(torch.uint8),
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__, "-v", "-s"]))

**[correctness, blocking] Non-finite inputs become fp8 NaN codes.** `__nv_fp8x4_e4m3(float4)` uses SATFINITE, which saturates ±inf/out-of-range but converts **NaN to an fp8 NaN code (0x7f)**. The absmax above uses `fmaxf` (IEEE drops the NaN operand), so `inv_scale` stays finite and NaN values sail straight into the packed codes.

Every kernel this path replaces (`silu_and_mul` + `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` — AOT v1/v2, Triton, and the unified kernel after #32188) clamps first: IEEE `fminf`/`fmaxf` return the non-NaN operand, so non-finite inputs quantize to ±448. CUDA-graph capture warmup runs the model over reused, uninitialized buffers; on CI runners those contain NaN bit patterns. Exactly this omission in #30924 broke the H100 deepep CI (`NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits`), root-caused and fixed in #32188 — and this kernel sits on the default Triton-runner path with the env flag default-on.

Fix (bit-identical for finite inputs): a single-sided `fminf(v, 448.f)` before packing is sufficient — see #32296 for the argument (min kills NaN/+inf, SATFINITE handles -inf). Also `scale = local_max / kFP8E4M3Max` (L134) can store an exact `0.0` scale for an all-zero group; the family computes `max(amax, eps) / 448` and never emits 0.0 — worth matching while here. Please also add a poison test mirroring `test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_non_finite_inputs_are_sanitized`.

**[correctness, blocking-ish] `__shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, ...)` with early-exited lanes is UB.** Two divergent `return`s sit above this (L89 tail, L92 expert filter). Whenever `hidden_dim % 256 == 128` (i.e. `num_vecs % 32 == 16`) a warp straddles two tokens, so half the warp can exit while the other half executes a shuffle whose mask names the exited lanes — undefined behavior per the CUDA programming guide, and `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` will flag it.

Note your own e2e config hits the shape: Qwen3-235B moe_inter 1536 / TP4 = 384 → `num_vecs = 48`. The minimal test shape `(1, 256)` hits it too (lanes 16–31 exit at the tail). It happens to produce correct results on sm90 because the xor-butterfly (masks 8/4/2/1) stays within each 16-lane half — that's luck, not contract, and it isn't guaranteed on future archs.

Suggested fix: keep all lanes alive through the reduce — follow the in-tree `per_token_group_quant` flat kernel pattern (warp-uniform exit + tail duplication via `min(work_id, total-1)`), or predicate the loads/stores instead of returning. Precedent for this bug class: #20661 (rmsnorm small-hidden fix).

**[PDL ordering]** `expert_ids` is read here, *before* `PDLWaitPrimary` (L99). With `enable_pdl(true)` this kernel may begin executing while the immediately-preceding kernel is still running; every dependent-data read must come after the wait. Today the preceding kernel is the Triton gate-up GEMM (produces `input`, which is correctly read after the wait) and `expert_ids` was produced earlier — safe by accident. Any reordering of the launch sequence turns this into a read of half-written data. Move the filter check below `PDLWaitPrimary`; zero cost. Same ordering rule as the masked `per_token_group_quant` kernel (wait precedes the `masked_m` read).

**[robustness]** The matchers pin shape/device but not dtype for `output_q`/`output_scale` (input does get `.with_dtype<T>()`). The kernel does raw pointer arithmetic assuming fp8/f32 contiguous rows — a wrong-dtype or non-contiguous buffer corrupts silently. Add `.with_dtype<fp8_e4m3_t>()` / `.with_dtype<float>()` and stride checks. Also `ActivationQuantParams.group_size` is dead in device code (the kernel hardcodes `kGroupSize = 128`) — drop the field or use it.

**[integration] Rebinding `intermediate_cache2` to fp8 has two downstream effects:**
1. `hooks.after_down(intermediate_cache2, ...)` (L805) now receives fp8 codes instead of bf16 activations when LoRA hooks are set — the `_use_fused_act_quant` gate doesn't exclude `hooks`. Either add `hooks is None` to the gate or confirm no hook consumes cache2 numerically.
2. The bf16 `intermediate_cache2` preallocated at L561 becomes a dead allocation on this path (`total_tokens * N/2 * 2` bytes allocated and dropped per layer/chunk). Hoist the `_use_fused_act_quant` decision above the allocation and skip it when the fused path will be taken.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces a fused activation and per-token-group FP8 quantization JIT kernel to optimize performance by avoiding extra global memory round-trips. It includes the CUDA kernel implementation, Python JIT bindings, integration into the Fused MoE runner sequence, and comprehensive unit tests and benchmarks. Feedback highlights a critical warp-synchronous undefined behavior in the CUDA kernel where early exits before a warp-wide reduction (`__shfl_xor_sync`) can cause GPU hangs on modern architectures; using an active flag to guard execution instead of early exits is recommended.

> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.

Reviewed the kernel and the Triton-runner integration in detail. The direction is right — this is a real memory round-trip on the Triton runner, and the DeepGEMM runner already has its fused counterpart. But there are two blocking kernel-level issues (one of which just broke the H100 deepep CI in #30924 in exactly this form, root-caused in #32188) plus a few integration hazards. Details inline; summary below.

**Severity order**: F1 NaN sanitization (blocking) > F2 shuffle UB on straddling warps (blocking-ish) > F3 PDL read ordering > F4 fp8 `intermediate_cache2` downstream effects > F5/F6 robustness & maintainability nits.

**Open questions**
1. Was `filter_expert=True` (EP) covered by any e2e run? The GSM8K config (TP4/DP2) has `num_experts == num_local_experts`, so the filtered path only has synthetic unit tests.
2. Any e2e throughput number (decode tok/s before/after) on a Triton-runner fp8 model? The PR shows kernel-level wins only; at decode batch sizes launch overhead can eat the round-trip saving.
3. Suggest landing with `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_ACT_QUANT` default **off** until F1/F2 are fixed and one full CI cycle has passed — this path is default-on for every fp8-block model on the Triton runner.
4. The branch predates #30924/#32072: `sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8` (your unfused reference) has since been rerouted to the unified JIT kernel, and file layouts moved. Please rebase and re-run the bit-exactness assertions.

**Test gaps**: (a) NaN/Inf poison test mirroring `test_per_token_group_quant.py::test_non_finite_inputs_are_sanitized`; (b) shapes with `hidden_dim % 256 == 128` (e.g. 128/384/1408) under filtering + a `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` pass; (c) `scale_ue8m0=True` has zero coverage and no integration caller — drop the axis or test it; (d) a capture+replay smoke test since the kernel launches with PDL inside decode graphs.
